description: ΔT = TT − UT1 in seconds at a given Julian Day (UT). Sourced outside this repository; NEVER regenerated by any tool here. Both engines' time bases rest on ΔT, so an error here moves every body without moving their agreement with each other — exactly the class of fault the golden vectors cannot see.

anchors.uncertainty_basis: The source prints 2 decimal places, so the true value lies within ±0.005 s of the printed figure by rounding alone. The source states no separate measurement uncertainty for the modern (atomic-clock) era, where ΔT is observed rather than modelled.
anchors.engine_allowance_note: Swiss Ephemeris interpolates its own ΔT table (Astronomical Almanac / IERS-derived, refreshed per swe release). Two correct implementations of the modern era can differ at the few-hundredths-of-a-second level from table vintage alone. 0.05 s is ~0.02 arcsec of lunar motion — far below the 0.01° longitude tolerance any chart output is held to, so this allowance cannot mask a chart-visible error.
anchors.source: NASA GSFC / EclipseWise Delta T tables (Espenak & Meeus, Five Millennium Canon of Solar Eclipses: −1999 to +3000)
anchors.citation: ΔT for the year 2000 is quoted as increasing from 63.83 sec on 1 Jan 2000 to 64.09 sec on 31 Dec 2000 (rounded value 64 seconds).
anchors.retrieval_note: Retrieved via search-engine extract of the source page; the page itself was unreachable from this environment's egress proxy (403). The two values were cross-checked against each other and against the era's published polynomial before being accepted — see ACQUISITION.md §Verification.

deferred.reason: The work order asks for ΔT at 1900, 2000 and 2050. Only the 2000 epoch had an exactly-quotable published value reachable from this environment (see ACQUISITION.md). 1900 and 2050 are specified there with their exact queries and are to be filled by a session with open network egress, or by the operator. Fabricating them from recollection was refused: a misremembered digit either red-bars a correct engine or sanctifies a wrong value, and the second failure is silent.
